title: DocumentReleaseAttachment
description: One enumerated attachment of one owning text body, and the renditions it was published in. The ROW is the attachment and the text body it becomes; the per-rendition SUB-ROWS are the renditions that succeeded or failed. Attachments are not members of the requested universe U — they are renditions of a member — so they get accounting rather than a retention floor: every attachment enumerated by its owner's source record gets a row, every rendition of it a sub-row with a disposition, and the build fails when an enumerated attachment has NO row, never when a row honestly says it could not be captured.

attachmentId.description: `stable_urn("document-release-attachment", {ownerTextBodyId, ownerKind, attachmentIdentity}, version=2)`. The preimage carries NO rendition ordinal: one row groups its M renditions, and an id that changed per rendition could not name the row that groups them. Re-enumerating an unchanged owner therefore re-mints the same id.

ownerTextBodyId.description: The one text body that enumerated this attachment. An attachment's owner is exactly one text body and never another attachment, so the graph is two levels deep and acyclic.

ownerKind.description: Which unpacking rule produced this row, so the source shape stays reversible: the live pipeline packs document attachments flat and comment attachments nested, and both unpack once, at ingest, into one record. Never `attachment`: an attachment does not own an attachment.

attachmentIdentity.description: The source's own stable identifier for the attached file, or the owner-scoped ordinal where the source supplies none. Part of the id preimage, so it must be stable across re-enumeration of an unchanged owner.

attachmentTitle.description: The title the source gave the attachment, or null. Non-null only where the nested packing supplied one; the flat packing carries no title, and inventing one would make the record irreversible.

textBodyId.description: The text body this attachment became, EQUAL to its own `attachmentId` — one body per attachment, and a second name would be a second identity for one thing. Null when no rendition was `text-captured`: an attachment whose renditions all failed is still enumerated and still accounted, it just carries no text.

textKind.description: Which kind of text body this row belongs to. Exactly TEXT_SOURCE_KINDS minus `metadata-field`: one text pipeline, three kinds.

representation.description: The one selected human-readable Unicode representation of this attachment, under the document body's representation rules unchanged, or null when `textBodyId` is null. Representation is SINGULAR in v2, which is why at most one rendition of an attachment may be `text-captured`.

excludedRanges.description: Representation ranges deliberately not searchable, under the document body's exclusion rules unchanged. Empty when this attachment carries no text. An excluded range is a SEARCH exclusion, never a redaction: its bytes stay in the representation member and a reader slices them out by offset.

renditions.description: One sub-row per rendition the source published this attachment in, ordered by `renditionOrdinal`. At least one: an attachment nobody published in any rendition was not enumerated.

reasonCode.description: Machine-legible reason for a disposition other than `text-captured`. SEALED as a bounded kebab-case string rather than as an enum: closing the vocabulary requires the real corpus, so the enum closure is a first-real-mint obligation and this bound is what holds until then.

rendition.description: One published rendition of the attachment: the thing that succeeded or failed. Anything but `text-captured` carries a `reasonCode` and a presentable `reason`, so loss stays visible rather than being accepted silently. A below-floor attachment rendition is `extraction-failed` and never blocks the build.

renditionOrdinal.description: Source order, dense and zero-based within this attachment. It lives HERE and not in the `attachmentId` preimage: the id names the attachment, the ordinal names its renditions.

mediaType.description: The media type the source declared for this rendition. Carried on the sub-row rather than read off `capture`, because an unfetched rendition has no capture and is still enumerated with the type it was offered under.

attachmentDisposition.description: CLOSED at four tokens, deliberately avoiding the catalog's `selected | excluded | deleted | unavailable | failed` vocabulary: an attachment disposition is not a catalog disposition, and reusing the words would invite a reader to join them.

capture.description: The captured bytes of this rendition, under the document body's capture rules unchanged, or null for `source-unavailable` — the one token that says the enumerated bytes were never fetched, and so the one under which no capture record can honestly exist.

reason.description: Prose fit to show a reader, beside the machine-legible code.

allOf.description: The bytes exist unless the token says they were never fetched.
Anything but `text-captured` carries both halves of its reason.

captureRecord.description: Links the captured bytes to the exact catalog snapshot, source item, source-issued version, and candidate rendition. Carries the acquisition wall clock, and every preimage excludes it: `documentStateDigest` is taken over `content` alone and no set digest names a capture field, so two byte-identical captures stay one release while the provenance a reader needs survives in the record.

catalogReleaseId.description: The pinned `SourceCatalog` snapshot's own `catalogId`. Same pattern as the root pin's `catalogId`, and checked against it: fixing one and not the other would make every capture row disagree with the root.

objectKey.description: Relative POSIX path of the immutable, digest-pinned member holding the exact captured bytes.

expectedSha256.description: The digest the catalog declared before capture, when it knew one. Non-null means it MUST equal `sha256`; the build fails otherwise.

acquiredAt.description: When the captured bytes were acquired, mirroring `CapturedFile.acquired_at`. Required: erasing acquisition time would destroy provenance the reader needs.

acquisitionStartedAt.description: When the acquisition attempt began, mirroring `CapturedFile.acquisition_started_at`, or null when the downloader reported no start. Written, never omitted.

representation.description: The one selected human-readable Unicode representation. Markup is not search text: this is visible text extracted before segmentation, and every offset in this release counts its UTF-8 bytes.

excludedRange.description: Reused from the document body unchanged, dotted `reasonCode` vocabulary included: the exclusion ledger is one vocabulary across all three text kinds, and the bounded `attachmentDisposition` reason code is a different one.
